d: The West Asia war is putting renewed pressure on global energy markets. Brent crude has crossed $110 a barrel, compared with roughly $70 to $80 before the conflict. Shipping costs have also surged, with Goldman Sachs figures cited in the source showing the cost of moving a barrel of oil rising from about $3 to more than $20. Asian markets have fallen sharply as investors worry about further attacks, unsafe shipping and prolonged shortages. Europe is now discussing a proposal that could ask households and businesses to reduce energy use if supplies tighten further.
